WYR_Circus_Djinni
Akabi is a djinni in Rivington during Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. He is a performer at the Circus of the Last Days in Rivington, located at X: -68 Y: -75 where he hosts a Spin the Wheel game.
“
APPROACH, UGLY ONE.
„
— Akabi, when he first greets the player character.

Involvement

When approached, Akabi invites the party to participate and Spin the Wheel for 500 gold,[1] loudly promoting the allure of winning the jackpot. Akabi magically rigs his game, guaranteeing that participants only ever get an item from one of the sixteen consolation prizes of questionable value, unless the party manages to cheat the djinn himself.

Winning the jackpot

A successful  DC 20 Perception Check reveals that Akabi is cheating, manipulating the wheel to ensure no one wins the jackpot.

He denies any accusations, offering the interacting party member to simply spin again instead. If provoked, Akabi uses  Careful What You Wish For on the talking party member, transforming them into a  Cheese Wheel for 20 turns. Akabi refuses to let anyone play who has been transformed by him in this way, but other party members may still participate.

To win the jackpot, a party member must pickpocket Akabi for his  Djinni Ring, without which he cannot rig the game. Bards can also distract Akabi ( DC 15 Performance Check) with either a joke or a well-timed fart and win the jackpot. However, stealing the ring or the Bard distraction permanently locks the party out of winning future consolation prizes.

Jackpot "prize"

Regardless of how the party member wins, Akabi becomes enraged and accuses them of cheating. He transports the talking party member, alone, to a Jungle in the distant land of  Chult. This is the only way to reach this area and to obtain the items within, notably the trident  Nyrulna and the ring  Band of the Mystic Scoundrel. Therefore, it is recommended that the party member chosen to win Akabi's jackpot be capable of heavy combat and / or stealth, to survive in the jungle. If obtained earlier, one may also give  Summon Us to the party member, so they can summon additional help. They should also be able to pick a lock on the chest that contains Nyrulna.

Akabi permanently closes down the game if one character wins the jackpot, all characters are turned to cheese, or if all consolation prizes are claimed by spinning the wheel 16 times.

It is not possible to obtain all 16 of the consolation prizes and the jackpot as he shuts down the game on the 16th spin. He does not award the jackpot on the final spin, if he still has his ring or the bard option is not used.

Inspiration

Winning Akabi's "game" earns the following inspirations:

  • ⁠A Grand Prize! ( Sage background)
  • ⁠Cheating the Cheater ( Charlatan background)

Consolation prizes

There are 16 possible consolation prizes from Akabi. Although some have utility, most are either useless or even harmful.

  • +1 Breastplate, a normal Breastplate. The description text reveals it is simply named "+1 Breastplate."
  • Bag of Moulding turns all inserted food into moldy and rotten versions.[2]
  • Boots of Very Fast Blinking grants a per turn free casting of  Misty Step as a  Bonus Action, and is arguably the most useful of Akabi's 'prizes', except the character is stripped naked down to their underwear on every use, with the stripped articles of clothing left on the spot the user teleported from.[3]
  • Comeback Handaxe, as of patch 5 it "comes back" to the party member who throws it, but hits them upon doing so.
  • Eternal Carafe of Wine (Or Sometimes Acid) inflicts the  Caustic Brine condition on its user, dealing damage.
  • Magical Walnut contains five walnuts for a total of ⁠10 Camp Supplies.
  • Reverse Rain Cloak makes the wearer permanently  Wet while worn. The wearer also has any accumulated blood and dirt washed away upon equipping due to the Wet condition.
  • Staff of a Mumbling Wizard, when equipped, gives the user a cantrip similar to  Fire Bolt, except it does not scale with the caster's level and always deals 1d10 damage. It has a 5% chance of instead spawning a  Fireball centered on the target with every use of the cantrip. Pairs well with the Reverse Rain Cloak.
  • Unlucky Thief's Gloves provides a +2 bonus to Sleight of Hand checks, and adds a piece of Charcoal to the wearer's inventory for each item they steal; after stealing 20 times, the next steal adds a  Burning  Coal Bucket instead.[4] Pairs well with the Reverse Rain Cloak.

The other possible prizes are miscellaneous items with no further function:

  • Akabi's Old Lamp
  • Definitely a Broom of Flying
  • Gem of Restitution
  • Lonely Left Boot of Elvenkind
  • Mirror of Ageing
  • Sharess' Caress Voucher
  • The Other Hand of Vecna

  • Any gold spent on spinning the wheel

Notes and references

  1. ↑ The 500 gold required for each spin of Akabi's wheel is first taken from the Traveller's Chest in camp, rather than any which may be in the inventory of the character speaking with him.
  2. ↑ These can still be used as camp supplies and can be stacked with each other if the supply value is the same. Drinks are immune to this effect.
  3. ↑ The inventory, equipped shield, accessories, weapons, and the Boots of Very Fast Blinking themselves are not affected, and stay with the user.
  4. ↑ While the description of this item intends for the charcoal to be a punishment, the charcoal can be sold for a small profit. There is a chance for a charcoal briquette to be added instead, burning the wearer and possibly forcing them to exit the pickpocket attempt.
